payload.root_cause: normalize_region() (pyshop/pricing.py:16-17) only strips whitespace and never lowercases the region code, while TAX_RATES (pyshop/pricing.py:8) is keyed by lowercase codes ('ca', 'ny', 'tx', 'or'). tax_for() (line 51) therefore looks up TAX_RATES['CA'], which does not exist, raising KeyError: 'CA'. Per docs/README.md, region codes are supposed to be case-insensitive, so the fix belongs in normalize_region (add .lower()).

payload.rationale: The root cause is that normalize_region() (pyshop/pricing.py:16-17) only strips whitespace and never folds case, while TAX_RATES (line 8) is keyed exclusively by lowercase codes ('ca', 'ny', 'tx', 'or'). tax_for() (line 51) uses normalize_region(region) as the lookup key, so 'CA' raises KeyError. Appending .lower() to the return value makes normalize_region produce lowercase keys matching TAX_RATES, satisfying both the documented case-insensitivity (docs/README.md) and the test expectations ('CA' -> 'ca', ' ny ' -> 'ny', 'OR' -> 'or'). This is the single smallest change that fixes the root cause; no other callers of normalize_region exist that would be broken by lowercase output.
